n: This psalm has two halves: God revealed in creation (vv. 1–6) and God revealed in his law (vv. 7–14). The skies themselves proclaim God’s glory and craftsmanship.

f.w: The heavens declare the glory of God

n: Each day passes the message on to the next, and each night shares knowledge with the next — a constant, silent sermon.

f.g: Literally “pours out” speech like a bubbling spring.

n: They use no words or language; no voice is heard — and yet their message is clear.

f.w: There is no speech nor language
f.g: Many read this as “they have no speech, no words; their voice is not heard” — creation speaks without words.

n: Their message goes out to the whole earth. Paul applied this to the spread of the gospel. In the heavens God has pitched a tent for the sun.

f.w: Their line is gone out through all the earth

f.g: A tent — the sun pictured resting at night before rising again.

n: The sun comes out like a joyful bridegroom from his room, or like a champion eager to run his course.

f.w: as a bridegroom coming out of his chamber

n: It rises at one end of the sky and circles to the other; nothing is hidden from its heat. So nothing escapes God’s presence.

f.w: there is nothing hid from the heat thereof

n: Now the law: God’s instruction is perfect, restoring the soul; his testimony is reliable, making the simple wise. Notice the six names for God’s word in verses 7–9.

f.g: Restoring or reviving the inner life.

n: His precepts are right and bring joy; his commandment is pure and gives light to the eyes.
Reverence for the Lord is pure and lasts forever; his judgments are true and completely righteous.

f.w: The fear of the LORD is clean

n: They are more desirable than the finest gold and sweeter than honey dripping from the comb.
God’s words warn his servant, and keeping them brings great reward.

f.w: in keeping of them there is great reward

n: Who can see all their own mistakes? David asks to be cleansed from faults he doesn’t even know about.

f.g: Hidden, unintentional sins — faults unknown even to oneself.

n: He also asks to be kept from willful, arrogant sins so they don’t rule him. Then he will be blameless and innocent of great transgression.

f.w: let them not have dominion over me

n: A beloved closing prayer: may my words and my heart’s thoughts please you, Lord, my Rock and my Redeemer.

f.g: Hebrew go’el — kinsman-redeemer; Latter-day Saints see Jesus Christ as the Redeemer.
